Appearance:
 Shri Khuzema Kapadia - advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Vishal Panwar - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.18/2024 dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station Rampura, District Neemuch (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363,
366-A, 376, 376(2)(n), 376(3), 323, 506 of IPC, 1860 alongwith Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Applicant is in custody since 07.07.2024.
2. As per prosecution story, it is alleged that applicant has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in this case the statement of the prosecutrix and her parents have been recorded before the trial Court, however, they have not supported the prosecution case and declared hostile.
Age of the prosecutrix is 15 years and 3 months and age of the applicant is 22 years.
Applicant is in custody since 07.07.2024 (completed 10 months).
Final conclusion
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12237 2 MCRC-18857-2025 of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned Government Advocate opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection,
however, fairly admitted that the prosecutrix and her parents have not supported the prosecution case and turned hostile.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as the statement of the prosecutrix and her parents, custody period of the applicant, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application stands allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant/accused be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the BNSS.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE sumathi Raju @ Rajendra @Rajudas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44974661/
